Upstream author: Timothy M. Chan
Unmodified source: sss-original.cc, downloaded 6 October 2026 from
https://tmc.web.engr.illinois.edu/sss.cc
Paper: A Minimalist's Implementation of an Approximate Nearest Neighbor
Algorithm in Fixed Dimensions, May 9, 2006.
https://tmc.web.engr.illinois.edu/sss.pdf
Earlier paper: Closest-point problems simplified on the RAM, SODA 2002.
https://tmc.web.engr.illinois.edu/ram_soda.pdf

The downloaded file carries an author/date comment but no explicit license.
No new license is asserted for upstream code.

Our competitor chan_sss is an adaptation for exact inclusive axis-aligned
rectangle candidate reporting in 2D. The current benchmark applies its exact
integer disk predicate in the timed reporting callback.
It is not the original approximate nearest-neighbor implementation and its
timings must not be attributed to the original implementation unchanged.

Retained ideas: one common random coordinate shift, implicit Morton/shuffle
comparison using XOR and less_msb, a sorted array, median recursion, common
endpoint quadtree-cell pruning, and Morton bounds from query corners.
Changes: enumerate all matching points rather than shrink a nearest-neighbor
radius; prune only geometrically disjoint cells; include boundary duplicates;
use uint64 intermediates for full uint32 input plus shift; std::sort and a
contiguous point vector replace qsort and individually allocated points;
per-object state replaces globals. No explicit spatial tree or extra index.
The shift is reproducible using mt19937_64 seed 12121 by default, independent
of the point/query seed. No ANN time guarantee is claimed for exact range reporting. The rectangle
index itself does not implement disk membership: the benchmark adapter does.
The dimensional adaptation is recorded in src/runner/dimensional/.
